knownLimitations: 0.4.0 is unreleased; default intervention.mode=off and 0.3.x recall behavior is unchanged.
off changes no injection but still persists applied baseline spoken/silent counts in the local policy store and traces; it does not apply policy advice or adapt thresholds.

must_speak is an automatic policy floor, not an upper bound on explicit user intent. Hard rules short-circuit as defer_explicit -> conflict -> greeting/meta -> must_speak -> no_candidates -> no_novelty -> heuristic. Explicit defer, including cue-level user_negated, may override automatic must_speak, keeps self/checkpoint loaded, and records reason=defer_explicit plus applied.action=defer. This input-level defer applies in every mode: off records v0-baseline / enforced:false with no policy warning; shadow injects defer instead of baseline and records no baseline wouldAction.
must_speak is not a 100% speak guarantee: with no candidate it degrades to checkpoint-only (silent + must_speak_unavailable + degraded) while self/checkpoint still inject.

conflict requires an explicit which-is-right question plus a conflict-group candidate; exact intent uses quote, otherwise detail. Bare statements such as records disagree / 不一致 do not trigger. no_novelty is an anti-repeat exception that only silences when all candidates were already injected and does not weaken maxSilentStreak/exploration for fresh candidates.
The alreadyInjectedIds fragment-ID alias table is process-local; old mf_... IDs from before a sidecar restart may not resolve. Source/record IDs remain valid.
Phase 3 (model) and Phase 4 (adaptive thresholds) are code complete with fake-gateway/unit evidence only, not a real-model quality gate.
No real-model smoke or golden-set evaluation was run: no local model on this host; the model planner is covered by fake-gateway tests.
The E2E uses a fake OpenAI-compatible provider; sidecar, plugin, capability, host and HTTP paths are real.
Console screenshots come from verify:console:ui fixture data and prove UI state only; real-sidecar trace fields are asserted separately.
Attribution is heuristic; this report proves the designed signals fire and persist, not long-term answer quality.
Only OpenCode outcome attribution is covered; DSH/Hermes and cross-device policy sync are out of scope.
Performance numbers come from the base commit on one non-idle developer host and are regression evidence, not an SLA.

Outcome notes are capped at 200 characters; an explicit defer is recorded as reason=defer_explicit and applied.action=defer; reset clears policy statistics and runtime streak/last-decision state only, never memory, traces or outcome history.
Existing trace queryPreview (redacted, <=200 chars) is retained from 0.3.x; the new policy state stores no query text.

fixedProductionIssues.summary: OpenCode plugin sends fragment IDs (mf_...) in alreadyInjectedIds, while the sidecar compared them with source/record IDs, so host-level already-injected dedupe could be ineffective.
fixedProductionIssues.fix: buildCandidates() now matches sourceIds and fragment.id and keeps a bounded in-process fragment-ID alias table; noveltyOf() checks fragmentId and sourceIds.
fixedProductionIssues.residual: The alias table is process-local; old mf_... IDs from before a sidecar restart may not resolve.

fixedProductionIssues.summary: Outcomes and policy counters used the policy decision instead of the applied intervention, so shadow silent advice could be recorded as missed/silent even though baseline spoke.
fixedProductionIssues.fix: Plugin attribution uses applied; /context exposes applied; policy counts are written once after assembly using applied action. Covered by the shadow E2E.

fixedProductionIssues.summary: A delayed outcome for a pre-reset trace could re-dirty the policy counters right after reset.
fixedProductionIssues.fix: submitOutcome() rejects traces created before policyResetAt with recorded=false and warning outcome_before_reset. Covered by R7/R8.
